ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Convert the system of inequalities into boundary lines and determine the directions: 2x-y-2>=0 is equivalent to y<=2x-2; x+2y-1>=0 is equivalent to y>=(1-x)/2; 3x+y-8<=0 is equivalent to y<=8-3x. Therefore the feasible region is enclosed by the three straight lines y=2x-2, y=(1-x)/2, and y=8-3x. Find the pairwise intersections: y=2x-2 and y=(1-x)/2 intersect at (1,0); y=2x-2 and y=8-3x intersect at (2,2); y=(1-x)/2 and y=8-3x intersect at (3,-1). These three points all satisfy the boundary conditions, the feasible region is a triangle, and x in the region is all positive. The slope of the straight line OM is k=y/x. Look at the three sides separately: on the side (1,0)-(2,2), y=2x-2, k=(2x-2)/x=2-2/x, x∈[1,2], monotonically increasing, and the endpoint slopes are 0 and 1; on the side (2,2)-(3,-1), y=8-3x, k=(8-3x)/x=8/x-3, x∈[2,3], monotonically decreasing, and the endpoint slopes are 1 and -1/3; on the side (1,0)-(3,-1), y=(1-x)/2, k=(1-x)/(2x)=1/(2x)-1/2, x∈[1,3], monotonically decreasing, and the endpoint slopes are 0 and -1/3. The interior of the region will not produce a smaller value than the boundary endpoints, so the slopes at the three vertices are respectively 0, 1, and -1/3, and the minimum value is -1/3.
